sources.title: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa 3.14
sources.edition: Desiraju Hanumanta Rao prose translation; site chapter numbering; commentary interspersed
sources.locator: 3.14, narrative verses 1–7 and 21–26 (site prose; verse numbering follows the corresponding Sanskrit text)

claims.subject: rama
claims.summary: While proceeding toward Pañcavaṭī, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa encounter Jaṭāyu; Jaṭāyu identifies himself as a friend of Daśaratha, and Rāma accepts and honors him.
claims.speaker: Narrator; Jaṭāyu identifies himself in reported speech
claims.note: This is Rāma's meeting with Jaṭāyu after Agastya's direction to Pañcavaṭī; the passage does not depict Jaṭāyu meeting Agastya.

claims.subject: jatayu
claims.summary: Jaṭāyu says that he was born from Aruṇa.
claims.speaker: Jaṭāyu, speaking to Rāma
claims.note: A source-local Rāmāyaṇa genealogy claim; this witness should not be merged automatically with other Aruṇa traditions.

claims.subject: jatayu
claims.summary: Jaṭāyu identifies Sampāti as his elder brother.
claims.speaker: Jaṭāyu, speaking to Rāma
claims.note: The passage also says they belong to Aruṇa's lineage.

claims.subject: jatayu
claims.summary: Jaṭāyu identifies himself as Śyenī's son.
claims.speaker: Jaṭāyu, speaking to Rāma
claims.note: The passage gives both this parentage and birth from Aruṇa; both statements are retained without reconciling their genealogy.

search_log.query: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya Kāṇḍa 3.14 primary prose translation Jaṭāyu Aruṇa Sampāti Śyenī
search_log.outcome: Inspected the 3.14 narrative translation. Added Rāma–Jaṭāyu encounter and Jaṭāyu's explicitly spoken lineage; excluded the page's introductory synopsis and editorial glosses.

search_log.query: Existing Agastya graph and epic expansion duplicate audit for Jaṭāyu and ancestry
search_log.outcome: Checked canonical graph nodes and claims plus research/agastya/expansion/epic.json; these Rāmāyaṇa 3.14 named-person claims were not already represented. Existing Agastya-to-Rāma/Pañcavaṭī evidence supplies the upstream path and is not duplicated here.

notes: Expansion focuses on named-person links within three edges of Agastya: existing Agastya-to-Rāma evidence, then Rāma-to-Jaṭāyu, then Jaṭāyu's parent and sibling links.
The 3.14 encounter is between Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Jaṭāyu, not between Agastya and Jaṭāyu. Shared itinerary is not represented as a direct meeting.
Aruṇa and Śyenī parentage are both stated for Jaṭāyu in this translation. The graph preserves both claims and makes no harmonizing identity hypothesis.
Site verse ranges are tied to the Sanskrit text represented by the prose page; editorial framing and commentary are not treated as primary narrative evidence.
